entries.summary: dict() builds a mapping from keyword arguments, and Rust keeps the order they were written in. This fork passes keyword arguments to functions and filters as a Go map (value.Callable, filters.Filter), so the order is lost at the call boundary, before the function can preserve it. Ordered map values fixed every other mapping surface; this one needs the callable signature to carry an ordered mapping.

The engine computes `a % b` on integers and PANICS on a zero divisor (tests.rs:153-159). The fork refuses with an invalid operation instead: a panic is not a behaviour worth reproducing, and answering `false` where the reference implementation aborts is the dangerous direction. Deliberate and permanent; see PATCHES.md.

minijinja's lexer has no `\U` string escape and rejects the literal with BadEscape; the Go port's lexer accepts Go-style escapes and renders the character. A lexer difference on the way to the builtin, not a builtin difference.

Nor does it have Rust's `\u{...}` form. Both engines reject the literal, but under different kinds: minijinja's lexer reports BadEscape, while the fork's lexer reads `\u` as Go's four-hex-digit escape and reports a located syntax error. A lexer difference, owned by the template and error surface.
